Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated properly:

- Primary workload: chat/chatbot for customer support + a smaller reranking job.
- Expected traffic: steady daytime usage with the following initial targets you mentioned and a few clarifying Qs below.

Questions / confirmation items:
1) Target TPS (requests/sec) at P95 you want us to design for? You mentioned mid-double digits during peak; can you confirm a number (e.g., 10-20 TPS)?
2) Average token mix: please confirm average prompt tokens and average response tokens (we heard ~40 prompt / ~180 response but want precise numbers).
3) Peak concurrency (simultaneous in-flight requests) --- you mentioned some batch workflows up to ~30 concurrent. Confirm whether 30 is peak.
4) GPU preference: any mandated instance family? You mentioned preferring A100 80GB on earlier calls --- confirm.
5) Compliance/networking: any additional egress/kms/audit log requirements beyond VPC peering?

Next steps: once you confirm the items above we'll put together a short Dedicated sizing recommendation (nodes, GPU type, suggested autoscale policy) and an initial cost estimate. I've attached a lightweight capacity template if you want to fill more granular RPS/hour by region.

Best,
Dylan

Thanks for the details, Dylan. Quick sizing recommendation based on the inputs:

Summary numbers (initial recommendation):
- GPU type: NVIDIA A100 80GB (customer preference; good fit for mix with long tail).
- Baseline cluster: 3 x A100-80GB nodes (each node provisioned for ~8 concurrent generation slots).
- Concurrency: 3 nodes x 8 slots = 24 native concurrent slots. With batching and queuing we can handle 30 peak with modest queuing (<200ms extra).
- TPS capacity: measured with their token mix (~255 tokens/request) we estimate ~12 TPS sustained at P95 on 3 nodes. Token throughput estimate ~= 3 nodes * (GPU token/s capacity) approximated to meet 12 TPS.
- Autoscale policy: add 2 nodes at 70% GPU utilization (so scale to 5 nodes on peak).
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for chat contexts (expected ~20% cache hit) which reduces cost and tail latency.
- Batching: target batching window 20ms, max batch size tuned to limit P95 latency to <800ms for median requests; tune dynamically during initial run.
- Long-tail jobs (1,200 tokens): route to a lower-concurrency, higher-memory pool (or to scheduled batch runs) to avoid impacting interactive latency.

Network / compliance notes:
- VPC peering recommended with private ENIs; we support customer-managed KMS and will surface audit logs to their logging endpoint. Retention policy can be configured to 1 year as requested.

Attachments: I exported a quick cost/sizing sheet (acme_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx) and network requirements (redwood_network_requirements.pdf).

If this matches, Rafael can draft a pricing & committed capacity proposal (monthly committed nodes + burst policy) and I can get the tech provisioning checklist ready.

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
